subject.title: Add guarded MCP coordination send route

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose two named internal coordination sessions through a dedicated public MCP and Gateway API, or should coordination writes be part of the generic capability-driven session surface?
rationale: The fixed session names, public Gateway method, generated native models, and special session-creation behavior establish a product and compatibility contract that cannot be selected safely from implementation evidence alone.

options.title: Generalize session writes
options.body: Fold the use case into the capability-driven MCP session API tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/103621 and keep coordination naming outside the public core contract.

options.title: Sponsor the fixed-key API
options.body: Keep the dedicated method, but first block raw `sessions.send` access to protected keys, document the contract, and require live fresh-install and upgrade proof.

options.title: Decline the core route
options.body: Close this implementation and keep coordination-specific naming and policy in its owning integration or operational workflow.

recommendation.title: Generalize session writes
recommendation.body: Fold the use case into the capability-driven MCP session API tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/103621 and keep coordination naming outside the public core contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest merged history for the MCP bridge, its Gateway client boundary, and its live Docker proof routes through this owner.
